clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 3 for the Avalanche fold: can an ordinary account make a PoolManager write land on, or a PoolManager read return, another user's entry?
clearedSpotChecks.note: The hook at avalanchego 983815fd vms/saevm/cchain/libevm/extstate/statedb.go lines 45-56 was fetched: TransformStateKey ignores the address and clears bit 0 of byte 0 (key[0] &^= 0x01), so the fold stays inside one account. A live eth_getStorageAt on api.avax.network at PoolManager 0x06380c0e0912312b5150364b9dc4542ba0dbbc85 returned the owner word 0x47eb0cf11a1626462da3c830bcde64c3f582b5a6 for both slot 0x0 and slot 0x01 followed by 31 zero bytes, and owner() returned the same address, so the fold acts on reads through the RPC too. In src, the only raw writes are tstore to fixed transient slots (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13,19, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:22,32, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:23,29-30, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:39), sstore at keccak256(wordPos, self.slot) in src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:67-73 and sstore to info.slot of a tick in src/libraries/Pool.sol:547; extsload and exttload only read (src/Extsload.sol:10-15, src/Exttload.sol:10-15). Every other persistent slot comes from Solidity mappings and fixed declarations, so a caller cannot choose an index. To reach a victim slot the attacker needs a keccak output that agrees with it in 255 bits. Against a set of N victim slots that is about 2^255/N tries, which stays infeasible. The fold also writes the asset partition with bit 248 set (assetBalanceKey, lines 58-62) while contract keys always have it cleared, so the two partitions cannot meet.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 4: live probe at the real PoolManager of all 21 networks with exttload and extsload of 20 indexes, comparing persistent and transient key spaces.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I recounted the rows in cycles/024/theme-storage-key-mapping.work/out/pmkeys.json. On every network all 20 transient reads equal expectT. On 20 networks the only persistent row that differs is slot 6, where expectS is null because slot 6 received no override, and the read is 0. On Avalanche 11 persistent rows differ, each one a bit 248 pair that reads one shared value, including slot 0 reading the override written to its partner and the balance slot 0x8f57... reading the partner marker plus the mint. That matches F-040 and the hook source above. The client strings before and after the call are present for each network.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 1 for Monad v0.16.5 and v0.16.7: TrieDb key encoding and page encoding of storage.
clearedSpotChecks.note: category/execution/monad/db/storage_page.hpp at v0.16.7 was fetched. PAGE_KEY_SHIFT is 7, compute_page_key returns the slot shifted right by 7, compute_slot_offset returns the low 7 bits of byte 31, and compute_slot_key rebuilds (page << 7) | offset. The map from slot to (page, offset) is a bijection, so two slots never share an entry. Whether whole pages read the same in the EVM and through eth_getStorageAt on mainnet is still the open Monad lead from the research file. I did not run it.
